# Ancient Greek {#sec-ancient-greek}

This is the prayer as it survives: Koine Greek, the common language of the
eastern Mediterranean, in which Matthew's gospel was written. Everything in
the other chapters is a translation of this.

The transliteration under each line is Wikipedia's scholarly romanisation. It
records the *spelling* rather than any one pronunciation — macrons mark long
vowels (η as `ē`, ω as `ō`), `h` at the start of a word is the rough breathing,
and the circumflex and acute mark the pitch accent. Read as reconstructed
Attic-Koine it sounds nothing like the Modern Greek chapter, though the letters
on the page are nearly identical.

## Critical text (NA28)

The text of the current Nestle-Aland *Novum Testamentum Graece* and the United
Bible Societies' *Greek New Testament*, which most modern translations follow.

::: {.prayer lang="grc" speech="el-GR" #grc-na28}
| πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
| [páter hēmôn ho en toîs ouranoîs]{.tr}
| ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου
| [hagiasthḗtō tò ónomá sou]{.tr}
| ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου
| [elthétō hē basileía sou]{.tr}
| γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς
| [genēthḗtō tò thélēmá sou hōs en ouranô(i) kaì epì gês]{.tr}
| τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον
| [tòn árton hēmôn tòn epioúsion dòs hēmîn sḗmeron]{.tr}
| καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν
| [kaì áphes hēmîn tà opheilḗmata hēmôn hōs kaì hēmeîs aphḗkamen toîs opheilétais hēmôn]{.tr}
| καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ
| [kaì mḕ eisenénkēis hēmâs eis peirasmón allà rhŷsai hēmâs apò toû ponēroû]{.tr}
:::

## Patriarchal Edition, 1904

The Byzantine-type text of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople. This
is the version actually prayed and sung in Greek Orthodox liturgy today, and
the one older English Bibles were translated from.

::: {.prayer lang="grc" speech="el-GR" #grc-1904 .variant}
| Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς,
| [Páter hēmōn ho en toîs ouranoîs,]{.tr}
| ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου·
| [hagiasthētō to onomá sou;]{.tr}
| ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·
| [elthétō hē basileía sou;]{.tr}
| γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
| [genēthētō to thélēmá sou hōs en ouranōi kaì epì tês gês.]{.tr}
| τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον,
| [tòn árton hēmōn tòn epioúsion dòs hēmîn sēmeron,]{.tr}
| καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφίεμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν.
| [kaì aphes hēmîn tà opheilēmata hēmōn, hōs kaì hēmeîs aphíemen toîs opheilétais hēmōn.]{.tr}
| καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
| [kaì mē eisenénkēis hēmâs eis peirasmón, allà rhŷsai hēmâs apò toû ponēroû.]{.tr}
:::

Three differences from the critical text are worth spotting: ἐπὶ **τῆς** γῆς in
the fourth line, **ἀφίεμεν** for ἀφήκαμεν in the sixth — present tense, "as we
forgive", rather than aorist, "as we have forgiven" — and the doxology
appended at the end:

::: {.prayer lang="grc" speech="el-GR" #grc-doxology .variant}
| ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. ἀμήν.
| [hóti soû estin hē basileía kaì hē dýnamis kaì hē dóxa eis toùs aiônas. amḗn.]{.tr}
:::

When a priest is officiating he uses the augmented form: *τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ
Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος· νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων*, and
the congregation answers *Ἀμήν*.

## ἐπιούσιον

The fifth line contains a word that occurs nowhere else in Greek literature
outside this prayer: *ἐπιούσιον*. It was coined for the translation, or it is a
term so ordinary that nothing else recorded it. Jerome rendered it
*supersubstantialem* in Matthew and *quotidianum* in Luke; English settled on
*daily*, which is a guess made comfortable by long use.

Most verbs in the first half of the prayer are third-person aorist passive
imperatives — *let your name be hallowed*, a form English can only reach
through paraphrase. The second half turns to second-person actives: *give*,
*forgive*, *deliver*.
